NONE: smidgen
› a very small amount
少量，一丁點兒

example: Could I have a smidgen more wine?
我能再來一點酒嗎？
It was five years since I'd last seen him, but he hadn't changed a smidgen.
我有五年沒見到他了，但他一點都沒變。

NONE: B1 a happy or friendly expression on the face in which the ends of the mouth curve up slightly, often with the lips moving apart so that the teeth can be seen
微笑，笑容

I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to make a happy or friendly expression in which the corners of your mouth curve up
T: › [ T ] to express or say something with a smile

example: Amy had a big/broad smile on her face.
埃米臉上滿是笑容。
She has a nice smile.
她笑得很甜。
He winked and gave me a smile.
他眨了眨眼，對著我笑了一下。
It's nice to be able to bring a smile to people's faces (= make people smile).
能讓人笑感覺真好。
He smiled and shook my hand.
他笑著和我握了手。
When he smiled at me I knew everything was all right.
他對著我笑時，我就知道一切正常。
Esme's so cheerful - she's always smiling.
埃絲米很開朗——她總是笑咪咪的。
I couldn't help smiling when I thought of how pleased she was going to be.
想到她會多麽高興時，我就忍不住要笑。
He smiled politely as Mary apologized for her drunken friends.
當瑪麗替她喝醉的朋友道歉時，他很有禮貌地笑了笑。
He smiled to himself as he thought about his new girlfriend.
想到自己的新女友，他會心地笑了。
He smiled the smile of a man who knew victory was within reach.
他露出了穩操勝券者特有的微笑。
He smiled his congratulations and left without another word.
他微笑著表示祝賀，然後就離去了，沒有再多說一句話。
"Don't you worry about a thing. Everything's going to be just fine," smiled Robin reassuringly.
「別擔心，一切都會很好的，」羅賓微笑著安慰道。

NONE: › to feel positive about something or someone, or to treat it, him, or her in a very positive way
積極對待

example: The government began to smile on small businesses when it realized that they were the key to economic growth.
政府意識到小企業是經濟增長的關鍵後，開始對其另眼相看。
figurative The gods smiled on us and we had brilliant sunshine throughout the day.
上天眷顧我們，我們度過了陽光明媚的一天。

NONE: › an emoticon (= a sideways image of a face, consisting of keyboard symbols, used in emails to express emotions)
（電子郵件中用鍵盤符號構成的）笑臉
› A smiley person or someone who has a smiley face looks friendly and smiles a lot.
笑容可掬的，笑容滿面的
› having a smile
微笑的，笑著的

example: I really miss seeing their happy smiling faces.
我真的好想念他們開心的笑臉。

NONE: › If you do something smilingly, you smile as you are doing it.
面帶微笑地

example: The child smilingly handed her a drawing he'd done.
孩子微笑著遞給她一張他畫的畫。

NONE: › a smile that expresses satisfaction or pleasure about having done something or knowing something that is not known by someone else
假笑；傻笑；得意的笑
› to smile in this way
假笑；傻笑；得意地笑

example: "Maybe your husband does things that you don't know about," he said with a smirk.
「你丈夫也許在做些你不知道的事情。」他詭秘地笑著說。
"I told you it would end in disaster," said Polly with a self-satisfied smirk on her face.
「我告訴過你這會是一場災難，」波莉臉上露出自得的笑。
I don't like the way he winks and smirks at me whenever he sees me.
我不喜歡他每次看到我時一邊眨眼睛一邊得意地笑。
He smirked his way through the interview.
整個面試過程中他都在得意地笑。

NONE: › to hit someone forcefully or to have a sudden powerful or damaging effect on someone
重擊（某人）；深深影響（某人）
› someone who makes things out of metal, especially by heating it and hitting it with a hammer
鐵匠，鍛工

example: a goldsmith/silversmith
金匠／銀匠
See also
blacksmith

NONE: › a lot of very small broken pieces
碎片，碎屑

example: The city was bombed to smithereens during the war.
城市在戰爭中被炸成了瓦礫。
So many films involve everyone and everything being blown to smithereens.
許多電影中都有人和東西被炸得粉碎的場景。

NONE: › a place where things are made out of metal, especially iron or steel, by heating and using a hammer
鍛冶廠，鐵匠鋪
› having suddenly started to like or love something or someone very much
突然迷上的，突然愛上的

example: The story's about a man smitten with love for his wife's cousin.
故事講的是一位男子突然愛上了他妻子的表妹。
He was so smitten by her that he promised to move to Argentina to be near her.
他對她太著迷了，以至於承諾要搬到阿根廷去待在她身邊。
